passage_text: Researchers investigated how temperature influences the activity of a purified enzyme involved in carbohydrate metabolism. The enzyme was incubated at five discrete temperatures (20°C, 30°C, 40°C, 50°C, and 60°C) in a buffer of constant pH. Activity was measured spectrophotometrically by monitoring the formation of a colored product over a fixed time period. Each temperature condition was run in triplicate to assess experimental variability. Activity is reported in U/mL. The resulting data revealed a bell‑shaped curve, with activity rising from 20°C to a peak at 40°C, followed by a decline at higher temperatures. The decline at 50°C and 60°C is consistent with partial denaturation of the enzyme, reducing catalytic efficiency. The findings provide insight into the optimal operating conditions for this enzyme and have implications for industrial applications where temperature control is critical.
stem: Which temperature had the highest enzyme activity?
explanation: The table shows the activity values; 9.5 U/mL at 40°C is the maximum.
trap: Assuming a linear increase across all temperatures.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the data?

options.A: Activity at 60°C was higher than at 20°C.

explanation: Correct: D) Activity ranged from 5.2 to 9.5 U/mL across temperatures, so temperature clearly affects it. Why the others are wrong: A) 6.3 at 60°C is higher than 5.2 at 20°C. B) The maximum, 9.5 U/mL, occurs at 40°C. C) Activity falls from 9.5 to 8.1 to 6.3 after 40°C.
trap: Assuming activity is unaffected by temperature because the values stay in a narrow-looking range, when 5.2 to 9.5 U/mL is a nearly twofold change.

stem: What is the percent decrease in activity from the peak at 40°C to 60°C?
explanation: Correct: A) (9.5 - 6.3) / 9.5 x 100 = 33.7%. Why the others are wrong: B) 50.8% divides the 3.2 drop by the 60°C value (6.3) instead of the peak. C) 66.3% is the activity at 60°C as a percent of the peak, not the decrease. D) 21.1% does not follow from the table values.
trap: Dividing the 3.2 U/mL drop by the final value (6.3) gives 50.8% (B), and reporting 66.3% (C) gives the remaining activity rather than the decrease.
